name: Polydactyly Induction
description: Induces growth of one or two additional fully functional fingers on each hand, positioned between the ring and little finger. The extra digits have full skeletal, muscular, tendon, and neural integration — they're not vestigial; they work. The brain's somatosensory and motor cortices must expand to accommodate the new digits, which requires a neural integration period of 3–6 months during which the extra fingers are clumsy and poorly coordinated. Users who complete integration report that the extra fingers feel natural — they can't imagine having only five. The modification is valued by musicians, surgeons, craftspeople, and anyone whose work benefits from additional manual dexterity. Six-fingered and seven-fingered pianists can play chords that are physically impossible for five-fingered hands. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's installation is the gold standard, with the fastest neural integration time.
source_organism: Synthetic polydactyly induction factors, Ailuropoda melanoleuca (giant panda, pseudo-thumb developmental pathway)
procedure: Hand surgery with retroviral digit induction and neural pathway expansion, 3 sessions per hand
expression_time: 4–6 months for digit growth; 3–6 months for neural integration
reversibility: Surgically removable; neural mapping changes persist — phantom fingers are common post-removal
side_effects: 3–6 months of reduced hand function during neural integration
Standard gloves, tools, and interfaces don't accommodate extra fingers
Phantom finger sensation if modification is removed
Increased risk of repetitive strain injury from denser tendon arrangement
Rare: neural integration failure resulting in permanently uncoordinated extra digits
social_perception: Fascinating and slightly unsettling. Six-fingered handshakes take people by surprise. Musicians and craftspeople with extra digits are respected for their commitment to their craft. In casual social settings, the extra fingers are a conversation piece.
story_hooks: A six-fingered surgeon is the only person in the district who can perform a specific procedure — and they've disappeared
A polydactyly induction starts producing fingers that don't stop — the growth factor is active and uncontrolled, and the user's hands are becoming something that doesn't look human
